findings.text: The manifest records neither a baseline_suite nor an after_suite arm, so the armed census pair this node's suite fence declared (tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py and tests/test_every_shared_home_lock_holds_across_nodes.py, 58 passed at both 42fe90d0b0a4 and 65efa64e1511) exists only as baseline-suite.log and after-suite.log with no manifest field pointing at it — and the done_when names 'both arms recorded as inline JSON carrying full 40-character revisions' as a required clause. reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:2265 returns a refusal clause when a manifest carries neither name, so promotion reads no observation to compute a delta against and this record cannot be promoted as written; the repair is to copy the two arms from the logs into the manifest, not to re-run anything.

The manifest carries two test_logs keys: line 13 is an empty field and line 14 carries the four real log paths, so a reader that takes the first occurrence (or splits naively) opens nothing on this line rather than the four logs the run wrote, which the write contract forbids by requiring exactly these keys.

The reviewed run recorded no rubric self-check: the manifest carries no rubric.<dimension> line for any of the six dimensions, which the worker contract states is reported as no self-check at all rather than as a passing one, and its artifacts, evidence_inputs, outside_scope and blockers keys are likewise absent, so the reconciliation fields promotion and the coordinator read are missing from a record whose status is complete.

The lint paragraph states 'ruff check reports one pre-existing F401 ... and ruff format --check reports the same two pre-existing spots at both' revisions, but no ruff log exists in the run directory and the manifest records no ruff command, so the done_when's 'ruff check and ruff format --check report nothing new on the changed paths' clause is prose with no receipt behind it; the claim is true — I re-ran ruff check on the base and head copies of tests/test_every_launch_route_runs_the_resolved_command.py and both report the same single F401 on the reckon.flight import at line 25 — but nothing in the run's artefacts lets a reader establish that without repeating the work.

notes: Durability is judged against the reinstated regression, not against a green run: restoring the removed misspelt path is not applicable here, the guarded shape is that tests/test_every_launch_route_runs_the_resolved_command.py:161 parses result.stdout rather than the combined output, and base-gate.log is that regression reinstated — the identical tree with the pre-change line parses the notice at preparation.py:1579 and reddens test_a_dispatch_runs_the_backend_command_it_resolved on json.decoder.JSONDecodeError, EXIT=1 — so the guard fires on the code shape it was added for. The converse regression, the product writing the notice back to stdout, also reddens the same line, because json.loads(result.stdout) raises rather than skipping. The change adds no assertion and removes none: 'run["ok"] is True' and 'str(bindir / COMMAND) in run.get("argv", [])' at :164-165 are pre-existing and are read against a value the product resolved (the fixture plants bindir on its declared search path while the launching PATH omits it), not against the variable the test handed in, so neither assertion moves with its own input. Score evidence at 13 because a done_when clause and the armed arm records are unmet on the record even though the underlying logs exist and were read: added_failure_count is 0, taken from baseline-suite.log's '58 passed' EXIT=0 at 42fe90d0b0a4 and after-suite.log's '58 passed' EXIT=0 at 65efa64e1511, with no failure ids on either side and per-test attribution unreadable at that resolution, so no id can be named as added. Re-ran nothing but ruff check on the two copies of the changed test file, to test the fragment's lint claim.
